description: Dillahunty argues that even witnessing a severed finger regrow would leave divine agency unproven until evidence connected that extraordinary result specifically to God.
critique: Strongest feature: By adopting Knechtle's laboratory example, Dillahunty sharply separates verification of finger regrowth from identification of its cause, granting that God remains possible while explaining why neither an extraordinary observation nor six historical sources supplies discriminating evidence of divine agency. Principal limitation: The hypothetical clarifies the inferential standard rather than applying it to the resurrection record, and it leaves unspecified what observable evidence could distinguish divine action from unknown natural causation or other proposed explanations. Live burden: Dillahunty must show cumulative indicia and multiple reports establish only an alleged anomaly without independently bridging it to God, while specifying a workable test for his demanded linkage. Locked score: 88 fits the exceptional burden contact and responsiveness, tempered by comparatively weaker evidential warrant.
